title: Waiting for the tap
objective: Recognize bacterial meningitis as an emergency and give antibiotics without delay while monitoring for raised intracranial pressure and septic shock

brief.situation: 20:00 in a medical ICU. You are Mr. Reid's nurse. He is 45, admitted 20 minutes ago from the emergency department with fever, a severe headache and confusion. A head CT is booked for 20:30 because he had a seizure in the ambulance; the lumbar puncture will follow.
handover: Ordered and on the unit: the ordered dexamethasone and two broad-spectrum IV antibiotics. The resident's note says 'hold antibiotics until after the LP so the cultures aren't sterile'.
Temperature 39.6 C on arrival; no blood cultures drawn yet.

Unit policy for suspected bacterial meningitis: blood cultures immediately, then dexamethasone with or just before the first antibiotic dose; antibiotics are never delayed for imaging or the lumbar puncture; neuro checks every 15 minutes; tell the intensivist of any concern.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated minutes per real minute. Pause any time.
Each assessment takes the time on its button. Decide what the findings mean, what to stop or start, and who must know.
Partway through you are asked to write your reasoning. A debrief scores what you did.

why.question: What is the emergency, and why do the antibiotics not wait for the CT and the LP?

parts.label: What
parts.criteria: Suspected bacterial meningitis: fever, severe headache, neck stiffness and confusion after an ear infection, with a falling GCS; watching for raised ICP and septic shock.
parts.modelAnswer: Fever, a bad headache, a stiff neck and confusion after an ear infection is bacterial meningitis until proved otherwise, and his GCS is dropping. He's also at risk of raised pressure in his head and septic shock.

parts.label: Why no wait
parts.criteria: Antibiotics are not delayed for imaging, the LP or the Gram stain; blood cultures first (fast); dexamethasone just before or with the first antibiotic dose; tells the intensivist to cancel the hold.
parts.modelAnswer: Treatment can't wait for a CT and LP that are half an hour away or more. Draw blood cultures now, give the dexamethasone just before or with the first antibiotic, and get the antibiotics in. I tell the intensivist so the hold is cancelled.

scoring.modelReasoning: Fever, severe headache, a stiff neck and confusion after an ear infection, with a falling GCS, is suspected bacterial meningitis: an emergency with risks of raised intracranial pressure and septic shock. Empiric antibiotics are not delayed for imaging, a lumbar puncture or a Gram stain. Draw blood cultures immediately, give dexamethasone just before or with the first antibiotic dose, and give the antibiotics now; tell the intensivist so the 'hold until LP' note is cancelled. Then neuro checks every 15 minutes and watch the blood pressure.
